core.title: Route every train an e2e test covers from a boundary route
core.given: An e2e test exists in the repository: a test file of the stack's e2e-test kind (per the profile: named as an e2e test and actually run by the stack's test runner), or any test file (any name) that carries the stack's train or journey binding marker.
core.when: the e2e test binds to a declared train
core.then: That declared train MUST be selected by at least one boundary route of the application.
prefer: Route the train from a boundary route so the application can actually reach it.
Or rebind the e2e test to a train that a boundary route already selects.
avoid: Keeping an e2e test green against a train nothing in the application can reach.
Renaming an e2e test away from the stack's e2e-test naming to dodge the check; a train or journey binding marker still classifies it.
unless: The e2e test is in a vendored or generated tree — never scanned (the profile's stack-wide exclusion list).
The bound train is undeclared — an undeclared binding is another rule's finding, not this one's.
core.why: An e2e test can stay green while exercising a train nothing in the application can reach; covering an unrouted train proves nothing about the product.
evidence: For every e2e test (existing or new), the declared train it binds to is selected by at least one boundary route.
The stack's e2e coverage check reports no covered-but-unrouted train findings.
verification: Recognition of an e2e test follows the profile: a file of the stack's e2e-test kind (name pattern AND actually run by the stack's test runner), or any test file whose header carries a train/journey binding marker — so a misnamed file is still judged, while a file that merely matches the e2e-test naming, is not run by the test runner and carries no marker does not qualify.
A lower-tier test (e.g. a unit test) that merely mentions a train or journey URN inside a string literal, without a binding marker, is not an e2e test.
Vendored and generated trees are never scanned; the exact excluded trees come from the profile's single stack-wide exclusion list.
Only declared trains are judged; a binding to an undeclared train is another rule's finding, not this one's.

The check cross-references the train each e2e test binds to against the selection made by all boundary routes, and is evaluated over the whole repository state: existing, unchanged violations are reported too, not only diff-introduced ones.

fires: An e2e test declares a binding to a declared train and no boundary route selects that train.
A test file not recognized by the stack's e2e-test naming still carries a train/journey binding marker binding it to a declared train that no boundary route selects.
An existing, unchanged e2e test binds to a declared train that no boundary route selects.
A boundary route is removed or changed so that a train still covered by an e2e test is no longer selected by any route.
doesNotFire: An e2e test binds to a declared train that at least one boundary route selects.
A unit test merely mentions a train or journey URN inside a string literal, without a binding marker.
A file matching the e2e-test naming that the stack's test runner does not run and that carries no binding marker.
The test lives in a vendored or generated tree (never scanned).
The test binds to an undeclared train (another rule reports that, not this one).

profileRequirements.meaning: What plays the e2e-test role in this stack, i.e. the recognition rule for an e2e test (browser-driving kind run by the stack's test runner, plus any marker-bound test file of any name).
profileRequirements.bunValue: browser_spec = a *.e2e.ts file run by Playwright, OR any test file of any name or extension whose header comments carry a journey marker

profileRequirements.meaning: Name patterns that flag a candidate e2e test file; necessary but not sufficient by itself (the file must also be run by the test runner or carry a binding marker).
The syntax by which a test file binds itself to a train (header marker), which also brings a misnamed file into scope.
The syntax by which a test file binds itself to a journey (header marker), which also brings a misnamed file into scope.
URN shape of a train, needed to recognize train references (e.g. a mere URN mention in a string literal is not a binding).
URN shape of a journey, needed to recognize journey references (e.g. a mere URN mention in a string literal is not a binding).
The stack's boundary route construct (the local name for what selects/routes trains) that the obligation is checked against.
How a boundary route selects the train(s) it routes, so a check can decide whether a given declared train is selected by at least one route.
profileRequirements.bunValue: each interlocking route carries selectors; a train is selected iff at least one interlocking route's selector selects it

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's test runner — here, the runner of the browser specs — and how to tell whether a given file is actually run by it; a name-pattern match alone does not qualify a file.
profileRequirements.bunValue: Playwright; a *.e2e.ts name counts only if the file is also run by Playwright (needs Playwright config/runner inspection)

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack-wide vendored and generated trees that are never scanned.

neutralityNotes: Browser spec is rendered as the e2e-test role; the runner-recognition branch (name pattern AND actually run by the stack's test runner) uses the existing tooling.test_runner profile key. 'Interlocking route' is rendered as boundary route; the local route kind (roles.boundary.kinds) and the selector-based selection mechanism (proposed idiom.routing#route_train_selection) are profile data. 'Declared train' is kept as-is: the core does not pin where trains are declared — every declared train a qualifying test binds to is judged. Bun sibling-rule, validator and finding ids stay bunOnly per the notProfileKeys policy.
